title: Camunda's business record is a mutable workflow instance whose history has a TTL and can be deleted
content:
Camunda's responsibility is sequencing — orchestrating when things happen. The durable business record it leaves is a mutable workflow instance: history is subject to a time-to-live, and instances can be deleted outright. Retention policy therefore determines how long the answer to "who decided this" survives, which is not the property an audit obligation needs.

The proposed seam keeps each system doing what it is built for. Powerhouse holds the append-only, user-attributed record of what was decided, and Camunda calls a Switchboard mutation at each decision point. The orchestrator loses nothing; the record simply stops depending on the orchestrator's retention configuration.

Five Camunda partners carry this finding, in DE, AT and SE, and four of the five are at priority 1 or 2. The same gap and the same seam are recorded verbatim for the Flowable cohort, which is the evidence that this is a property of BPMN engines as a category rather than a defect of one product.
